 th Order No. 03/Dated: 10 April, 2024  Heard learned counsel for the parties.

Apprehending his arrest in connection with Raneshwar P.S. Case No. 10 of 2023 registered under Sections 498A and 34 of the I.P.C., the petitioner has moved to this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.
As per FIR, informant of the case briefing that the marriage of the informant was solemnized with the petitioner on 08.12.2022, according to Hindu rites and customs.
It is alleged that her father-in- law had demanded additional dowry of Rs. 8,00,000/- from her father, but her father was unable to pay the same.
It is further alleged that on the first night, the petitioner refused to establish physical relations with the informant and stated that he loves one Puja Majhi and wants to live with her.
Ultimately, she driven out her matrimonial home.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all rather he has been falsely implicated in this case.
Petitioner undertakes to abide by all terms and conditions, as imposed by this Court, in the event of granting anticipatory bail to him.
Hence, the petitioner may be extended the privilege of anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: petitioner approached to the house informant, soon his greedy temperament raised seeing the car registered in the name of the informant and asked to inform her father to transfer the car and landed property after partition with his co-sharers in his favour.

He has also kept a concubine;
hence, the petitioner does not deserve anticipatory bail.
In reply, learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that Puja Majhi is cousin of petitioner and he has no illicit relationship with her.
Due to suspicion without any basis such type of amputation has been levied against the petitioner.
Petitioner is cooperating in the investigation in compliance of notice under Section 41(A) of Cr.P.C. and undertakes to further cooperate with the investigation of the case.

Considering the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of allegation against petitioner coupled with materials available on record and matrimonial dispute between the parties and also in view of the fact that the petitioner is cooperating in the investigation, I feel inclined to extend the privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

Accordingly, the petitioner is directed to surrender in the Court within four weeks from today and in the event of his arrest or surrendering, he will be enlarged on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Twenty five thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Dumka in connection with Raneshwar P.S. Case No. 10 of 2023 with the condition that he will co-operate with the trial of the case and will furnish his mobile number and photocopy of the Aadhar Card with an undertaking that he will not change his mobile number during the pendency of the case and subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
